p-6804.label: Overview
p-6804.content:
## Project purpose
The project builds a SaaS "Jira cockpit" that orchestrates AI agents to draft, refine and audit Jira user stories, turning raw needs (text, PDF and image attachments) into dev-ready backlog items. It targets product owners, business analysts and delivery teams who lose time and quality in manual backlog refinement and story writing.

## Functional scope
- AI agent pipeline — Dev Ready agent producing implementation plans, chained with a Dev Readiness judge
- Raw needs ingestion — capture of user needs, including PDF/image attachments
- Story authoring and refinement — "to author" and "to refine" cards, PO/BA versioning, diff views
- Dashboard and analytics — KPIs with period selection, AI telemetry (tokens, latency)
- Users, roles and access control — multi-account login, app-admin vs project-member gating

p-6804.label: Confluence
p-6804.content:
## Confluence space CASH
- *Payment lifecycle*: statuses of a payment from creation to bank settlement.
- *FX rates policy*: daily ECB rates, rate date stored with each conversion.
- *Performance targets*: dashboard under 2 seconds with 100 000 transactions.

p-6804.label: Codebase
p-6804.content:
## Stack
- Front: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui
- Back: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL

## Main modules
- `src/agents/` — one module per agent (authoring, refinement, spec, review)
- `src/api/` — REST endpoints used by the front
- `src/integrations/` — Jira, Confluence and GitLab clients

## Conventions
- Every agent output is a Markdown document stored with its sources.

p-6804.label: Jira
p-6804.content:
## Jira project TCAAS6804
- Issue types: Story, Epic, Bug, Task, Spike
- Workflow: To do → In progress → Review → Done
- Stories are linked to an epic through "Epic Link".

## Writing conventions
- Titles start with a verb.
- Acceptance criteria use Given / When / Then.
